research_concepts: foul and free-throw contamination of possession outcomes
methodological_questions: Is opponent next-possession PPP after play X large enough to justify an AVOID label?
Do own-sequence lagged possession outcomes add information beyond the current play type?
Do inferred play-type labels pass accuracy and distribution audits well enough to support downstream PPP comparisons?
How do foul, free-throw and assisted-flag leakage affect PPP by play type?
What sample size is needed to detect downstream effects of about 0.01 to 0.02 PPP?

historical_evidence.finding: Records a defensive aftershock and a sequential pair premium across 8 of 8 play types, replicated in all-games and playoffs (for example CUT +0.119 n=21,398; PO +0.131 n=1,145). Top pair premium PUTBACK->TRANSITION +0.084 n=565. The record notes a small-sample limitation. This concerns offensive pair premiums and aftershocks, not AVOID-label thresholds.

Extended Possession Value: 4 of 8 play types show a real downstream opponent next-PPP component (CUT +0.0220 suppression, TRANSITION +0.0145, SPOT_UP +0.0124, POST_UP +0.0194). DRIVE downstream is not real (opponent ATT +0.0024). Most player-level downstream effects are non-significant after Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) correction. Effects are about 0.01 to 0.02 PPP, small relative to direct PPP gaps.

Superstar sequential suppression: PUTBACK is the top opponent suppressor for 6+ stars (for example D. Mitchell 1.178 to 0.884, d=-0.294, n_after=95; B. Beal d=-0.345, n=32). Other top effects are small (TRANSITION A. Davis -0.058; POST_UP N. Jokic -0.075). Several cells have n_after of 32 to 95 and no multiplicity correction was applied.

Play-type PPP across playoff series game buckets (1,197 records, no CIs). DRIVE 0.889 to 0.949 (+0.060); CUT +0.114; PNR +0.087; PULL_UP -0.077; POST_UP -0.032. Recorded as 'NO CLEAR SIGNAL'. Observational, with selection caveats.

Play-type label accuracy and distribution audit, overall FAIL: OTHER is 20.2% against a target under 10%; 40.8% of labels are low confidence; DRIVE foul-draw rate 1.7% against a 14 to 22% benchmark; most play types have PPP above the benchmark band; MIA identity checks fail. Recorded verdict: tool_eval_fail.

OTHER: 36% of possessions end in fouls, which inflates PPP (FOUL_BUCKET). DRIVE is 12 pp below the foul benchmark (FOUL_LEAK). PNR foul rate is 22%. Only 335 of 50,668 possessions (0.7%) map to a real play type via initiation_type.

The assisted flag exists only on makes, so SPOT_UP PPP showed 2.83 (100% makes) and TRANSITION 0.62. After the classifier was rewritten, SPOT_UP was about 1.16 and TRANSITION about 1.20. Recorded as a construction artifact that had poisoned a simulation.

On-ball defensive scheme labels (DROP/ICE/SWITCH). Confident labels cover 14.9% of DET possessions (10 of 67) and 3.3% of ORL (2 of 60). The switches_on field was not populated by the NBA matchups feed.

Defensive scheme change within and across games using inferred labels: within-game change 61.0%, cross-game change 67.7%, and 99.0% of units change. Transition matrices are near-uniform, which the record describes as consistent with label noise. The inferred label cannot separate defensive adjustment from offensive execution.

Foul-trouble sequencing: raw lag-1 ATT +0.204 (CI [+0.163, +0.245]) was driven by a free-throw share of 41.8% in treated possessions versus 9.9% in controls. Excluding free throws, lag-1 is +0.0486 (CI [-0.0060, +0.0991], permutation p=0.0655). Lags 2 and 3 are negative. No lag clears CI, permutation and placebo together.

failed_approaches.why: The assisted flag existed only on makes, so the label leaked the outcome. Recorded as artifact_found (C_artifact).

failed_approaches.why: Foul endings inflated OTHER PPP by 36%, DRIVE was 12 pp below the foul benchmark, and initiation_type mapped only 0.7% of possessions. Recorded as artifact_found (C_artifact).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Play-type label accuracy and distribution audit against benchmarks.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Opponent next-possession PPP after a star's second foul, including free throws.

evidence_establishes: Downstream opponent next-possession PPP effects for some play types (CUT, TRANSITION, SPOT_UP, POST_UP) are reported as real in aggregate, at about 0.01 to 0.02 PPP (FAM:SF-APPS-075).
The reported size of these downstream effects is small compared with direct PPP gaps between play types (FAM:SF-APPS-075).

Several earlier PPP-by-play-type results were artifacts from label construction: assisted-flag leakage, foul-ending contamination, and free-throw confounding (FAM:SF-PAP-096, FAM:SF-CHT-025, FAM:SF15).
The play-type label pipeline failed its accuracy and distribution audit in at least one tested setting (FAM:SF-APPM-014).
Within the retrieved records, lagged own-sequence and pair-premium effects have been reported (FAM:SF07, FAM:SF-APPA-050), but these are not tests of AVOID-label thresholds.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether opponent next-possession PPP after play X is large enough to drive an AVOID label: no record tests a decision threshold for AVOID labels.

Whether the current 2026-06-19 label pipeline (including the rewritten play_type_inferrer and the derived graph records) passes audit, since the retrieved audit records predate or do not cover the current version.
Whether downstream effects survive exclusion of free throws and foul-ending possessions across all play types, since most records do not report this.
Whether 2025-26 data (partial before 2026-04-13 and the playoffs partial before 2026-06-21) can serve as a clean holdout.
Whether any effect holds after multiplicity correction across play types, lags and players; several records report no correction (FAM:SF-APPA-050).
own_inferences: The AVOID-label question as posed bundles two claims: a downstream effect exists and it is large enough to act on. Historical records support neither under current labeling, and the reported effects (about 0.01 to 0.02 PPP) are at the scale of label-induced artifacts.

Detecting a 0.01 PPP difference with per-possession point SD near 1 would need on the order of 20,000 possessions per group for a standard error near 0.01 (my calculation, not from any record). Per-cell n in the retrieved records (30 to 95 for several stars) is far below this.
Historical results do not say whether the 2026 labeling code has the same defects; the audit results may be stale.
The question can be partly answered after label repair, by estimating the downstream effect in a restricted, audited set of play types with free throws and fouls excluded.
uncertainties: The retrieved records do not include sample sizes or CIs for most aggregate downstream effects (FAM:SF-APPS-075 gives no explicit n).
The status of FAM:SF07 as supported rests on A2 aftershock replication; its overlap with FAM:SF-APPS-075 and FAM:SF-APPA-050 is unclear, and some records overlap in slices.
No record reports whether the rewritten classifier (after FAM:SF-PAP-096) has passed a re-audit.
No record gives a validated threshold for AVOID labels or a loss function, so the 'large enough' criterion is undefined.
Retrieval returned 10 records; other relevant families may exist and were not searched (search_documents was not called).

historical_effect.explanation: Before retrieval, the question looked testable with the per-game files and derived graph records. The retrieved history shows: (1) label construction repeatedly produced artifacts (FAM:SF-PAP-096, FAM:SF-CHT-025, FAM:SF15); (2) the label audit failed (FAM:SF-APPM-014); (3) reported downstream effects are small (FAM:SF-APPS-075); and (4) no record tests the AVOID-label threshold. Together these move the decision from proceed to do_not_proceed as posed, with a narrower minimum viable test specified below.

blocking_constraints.text: Play-type labels failed audit (OTHER 20.2%, 40.8% low confidence, foul leakage), and initiation_type mapped only 0.7% of possessions. Downstream PPP by label is unreliable until the pipeline passes re-audit.
Free-throw and foul-ending possessions drive the apparent effects (FAM:SF15: raw +0.204 vs +0.049 after exclusion), so the estimand is confounded by fouls unless these are removed.
Effects of about 0.01 to 0.02 PPP require roughly 20,000 or more possessions per comparison group; per-cell n for many star and play-type cells is 30 to 95 (FAM:SF-APPA-050).
Multiple play types, lags and players are tested; several records apply no correction (FAM:SF-APPA-050) or only BH at player level (FAM:SF-APPS-075).
The AVOID label is defined from the same next-possession PPP it is meant to explain, so the label and outcome are not independent.

prior_work.summary: Prior work partly addresses the downstream and own-sequence components: small aftershock and pair-premium effects are reported (FAM:SF07, FAM:SF-APPS-075, FAM:SF-APPA-050), but these are not tests of AVOID-label thresholds, and several results are flagged as artifacts or are underpowered. The label-quality prerequisite has repeatedly failed (FAM:SF-APPM-014, FAM:SF-CHT-025, FAM:SF-PAP-096). No retrieved record tests whether opponent next-possession PPP after play X is large enough to drive AVOID labels.

risks.text: Labels failed audit in the retrieved records; the rewritten classifier has not been shown to pass re-audit.
AVOID labels defined from next-possession PPP are circular with the outcome they are meant to predict.
Foul and free-throw contamination inflates effects (FAM:SF15, FAM:SF-CHT-025), and a play-type label may proxy for team or lineup.
Assisted-flag and make-dependent labels leak the outcome (FAM:SF-PAP-096, FAM:SF-APPM-014); any label that uses the same or later possession points is leaky.
Per-play-type and per-player cells are small (FAM:SF-APPA-050, n_after 30 to 95), and the implied effect size needs very large samples.
Play types such as PUTBACK and DRIVE have sparse foul-draw and make counts; several benchmark cells are sparse (FAM:SF-APPM-014).
Multiple play types, lags and players without correction (FAM:SF-APPA-050); BH applied only in part (FAM:SF-APPS-075).
Base rates of foul endings and free throws differ across play types; the foul benchmark used in FAM:SF-CHT-025 may not hold for all play types.
Possessions that end in a foul or with limited shot opportunity have a structural PPP floor or ceiling, so PPP differences partly reflect possession type rather than efficiency.
Playoff and regular-season effects differ (FAM:SF07, FAM:SF-APPS-010), and the 2025-26 playoffs are partial before 2026-06-21; a time-split holdout is needed.
Graph-database derived records and the play_type_inferrer rewrite have a history of bugs (FAM:SF-PAP-096), so the current code path must be verified before analysis.
Lag effects are sensitive to placebo and permutation choice (FAM:SF15 shows no lag clears CI, permutation and placebo together).

design.estimand: Minimum viable test: the difference in opponent next-possession PPP after own play X (or after the opponent's play X), relative to matched baseline, for play types that pass the label audit, with fouls and free throws excluded. The AVOID-label threshold is not estimated here; it must be pre-specified separately.
design.unit: Possession (opponent next-possession PPP conditional on the preceding possession's play type), with lags 1 to 3 kept separate.
design.sample: Estimation: NBA 2022-23 through 2024-25 regular seasons and playoffs. Holdout: 2025-26 regular season from 2026-04-13 onward (complete data only). Exclude 2025-26 playoff games before 2026-06-21 (partial). Exclude possessions with free throws or foul endings.
design.power: Run a power calculation before analysis for effects of 0.01 to 0.02 PPP. Per my own calculation (not from any record), a standard error near 0.01 requires on the order of 20,000 possessions per group; per-cell n in the retrieved records (30 to 95) is far below this, so only pooled play-type comparisons are plausibly powered.
design.controls: Exclude free-throw and foul-ending possessions; stratify by score margin, period and clock; include team and lineup fixed effects; use label-audit pass as an entry condition; compare against a matched baseline of the same play type without the preceding opponent play.
design.falsification: Placebo lags (lag 0 and lag -1) and permuted play-type labels should show no effect; the effect should vanish after free-throw and foul exclusion if it is an artifact (as in FAM:SF15).
design.multiplicity: Pre-specify play types and lags; apply Benjamini-Hochberg across play types and lags; report uncorrected and corrected results.
design.decision_rule: Treat an effect as real only if its confidence interval excludes zero after foul and free-throw exclusion, survives permutation and placebo checks, and passes BH correction. Do not derive AVOID labels from it unless a separately pre-specified threshold is met and the label audit passes.
design.data_version: Per-game NBA stats API files as of 2026-06-19, with the rewritten play_type_inferrer and derived graph records version-locked and recorded. Re-run the label audit on this version before any estimation.

methodological_questions: Can opponent next-possession PPP after play X be estimated reliably enough to drive AVOID labels?
Do own-sequence lagged possession outcomes add information beyond the current play type?
How do label derivation from outcomes and small exposure counts threaten validity?
What confounding and leakage risks arise when labels are built from points scored on the same or subsequent possessions?
